He mentions that they were under the rule of the Almohad Caliphate during the 13th century, but later fell into disunity and were conquered by the Marinids.
historical_references.context: The Zaluj were a Berber people living in North Africa during the medieval period. They were first mentioned by Ibn Khaldun in his 'Muqaddimah', where he described them as inhabiting an area corresponding roughly to modern Algeria and Morocco. The Zaluj were initially under the rule of the Almohad Caliphate, but later fell into disunity and were conquered by the Marinids.

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi in his 'Khitat' writes that the Zaluj were a Berber tribe that ruled over the Maghrib (North Africa) from the city of Tlemcen.
